newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK PM SAYS GUARDS NOT INVOLVED IN CYPRUS SHOOTING.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PM SAYS GUARDS NOT INVOLVED IN CYPRUS SHOOTING.

text.p: The guns of Greek-Cypriot guards were checked on Sunday after a Turkish Cypriot soldier was shot dead in Cyprus but none had been fired, Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis told a news conference.
"According to the Cypriot defence ministry, the weapons of the Greek Cypriot guards were checked and no weapon had been fired," he said.
"The conclusion of the Cypriot government is that no action was taken from the Greek Cypriot side which could have led to this result (the killing)," he added.

Tensions have risen in the last month following the killing of two Greek Cypriots by Turkish security forces and civilians in Turkish occupied areas during demonstrations against the division of the island.
Simitis, speaking at a long-planned news conference, said his information came from Cypriot officials, the Greek embassy and Greek Defence Minister Gerassimos Arsenis.
According to his information, one Turkish Cypriot soldier was killed and another wounded near the U.N.-patrolled buffer zone separating Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
Simitis said the reason for the shootings was not known but added "it may be an internal Turkish Cypriot community matter".
The shooting occurred at a Turkish Cypriot guard unit in the village of Acheritou, which Turks call Guvercinlik. It is on the northern edge of the British base of Dhekelia in southeastern Cyprus.
"A Turkish soldier was shot and killed about two miles east of Ayios Nicolaos," said Captain Sean Tully, spokesman for the British bases in Cyprus. "So far the incident is shrouded in mystery."
